title: code_index.extract_function request
description: Lift one expression, a run of whole statements, or a closure body out of a function into a new function `new_name`, and replace it (and, with `all_occurrences`, every same-file copy with an equal token sequence and the same bindings) with a call. Inputs are the region's free names bound in the enclosing function; outputs are names the region assigns that are read after it. Name the region by `start_line`/`end_line` or by its exact text in `region`. Rust, TypeScript/TSX, JavaScript/JSX, Python. All-or-nothing: every refusal leaves the file byte-identical.

path.description: File holding the region, relative to the indexed workspace root (or absolute).

start_line.description: First line of the region, 1-based. Leading and trailing whitespace on the selected lines is ignored.

end_line.description: Last line of the region, 1-based and inclusive. Defaults to `start_line`.

region.description: Exact text of the region, used instead of line numbers. Text that occurs more than once is `ambiguous_symbol` unless `all_occurrences` is set, in which case every match is a copy.

new_name.description: Name of the new function. Refused with `name_conflict` when it already appears in the file.

signature.description: Typed header of the new function, e.g. `fn parse(line: &str) -> Option<Job>` or `function parse(line: string): Job[]`. Its name must equal `new_name` and its parameter names must equal the computed inputs, in any order; the call passes arguments in signature order. Required for Rust and for strict TypeScript whenever the function takes or returns values.

helper.description: Escape hatch: the complete helper function, inserted verbatim after the enclosing item. Its name and parameter names are checked like `signature`; every copy of the region becomes a call to it.

all_occurrences.description: Also replace same-file copies with an equal token sequence and the same inputs and outputs. Defaults to true.

dry_run.description: Plan and validate without writing; the result is `applied` with `dry_run: true` and `applied: false`. Defaults to false.

session_id.description: Optional staged-fs session id; reads and writes go through the session overlay.
